sources.title: Property Assessment Data (Current Calendar Year)
sources.licence: City of Edmonton Open Data Terms of Use
sources.unit: one assessed residential property (a house, a townhouse, a condominium unit or an apartment building)
limitations: Apartment buildings are one account each; their homes are estimated from gross floor area at 185 m² per home, calibrated on 2021 Census households (checked in apartment neighbourhoods such as Downtown and Wîhkwêntôwin).
Properties assessed under $40,000 are left out (mostly parking stalls and storage units).
transformations: each property placed at the point the City publishes for it
apartment buildings (other residential) count as their gross floor area divided by 185 m² per home (an estimate, calibrated on 2021 Census households by neighbourhood)
8,141 properties with no year built (no building) left out
3,647 apartment buildings counted as 68,512 homes, estimated from floor area (185 m² per home)
7,087 records with no neighbourhood code placed by location; 0 fall outside every neighbourhood

limitations: Volunteer-mapped: coverage is uneven, and a missing feature means nobody has mapped it.
Only features not already in the city's inventory are added (matching rules in the method).

sources.title: 2021 Federal Census: Population
sources.licence: City of Edmonton Open Data Terms of Use
limitations: Counts are as of May 2021; growth since is not included.
Statistics Canada rounds counts, so neighbourhoods may not add exactly to the city total.

Neighbourhoods renamed, renumbered or split since the census (for example Oliver, now Wîhkwêntôwin) are matched by the census-day boundary: their residents go to today's neighbourhoods in proportion to the homes inside it that were built before 2021.
transformations: each area's residents and children spread evenly over its dwelling units
Oliver (1150, a code no longer in use): 18,695 residents placed in Wîhkwêntôwin (100%) by the homes inside its census-day boundary
Horse Hill Neighbourhood 1A (2691, a code no longer in use): 630 residents placed in Quarry Ridge (100%) by the homes inside its census-day boundary
Chappelle (5462, a code no longer in use): 10,910 residents placed in Chappelle (100%) by the homes inside its census-day boundary
Heritage Valley Town Centre (5464, a code no longer in use): 1,220 residents placed in Heritage Valley Town Centre (100%) by the homes inside its census-day boundary
children aged 0 to 14 from 2021 Federal Census: Age and Gender

children for new residents at 25.0%, the share in areas mostly built in the ten years before 2021
